name: source-serif-sans
why: Adobe designed Source Serif as a companion to Source Sans, so proportions and color agree while the 18th-c transitional serif adds a clear heading/body distinction.
caution: Both are restrained; add color or scale contrast so the page does not feel flat.

name: ibm-plex-serif-sans
why: Plex Serif and Plex Sans share one skeleton and x-height, so swapping roles never disturbs rhythm; serif headings add authority over a neutral grotesque body.
caution: Max weight is 700; do not expect a black weight for posters.

name: ibm-plex-mono-sans
why: Monospaced headings signal 'code/engineering' while Plex Sans keeps body copy readable; same-family metrics keep them aligned.
caution: Keep mono headings short; long mono lines get wide and slow to read.

name: noto-serif-sans-global
why: Noto is designed for harmonised coverage of most of the world's scripts, so this pairing survives translation without fallback-font mismatches.
caution: Load the script-specific Noto family (e.g. Noto Sans JP) for non-Latin text; the base families do not contain CJK/Arabic/Indic.

name: noto-serif-jp-sans-jp
why: Mincho headings over gothic body is a conventional Japanese editorial contrast, and both come from the matched Source Han/Noto CJK project.
caution: CJK fonts are large downloads; subset or limit weights.

name: noto-sans-arabic-single
why: A single family with weight contrast keeps Arabic UI consistent; Noto Sans Arabic is harmonised with Noto Sans for mixed Latin text.
caution: For traditional long-form Arabic, Noto Naskh Arabic reads more conventionally than this unmodulated sans.

name: roboto-slab-roboto
why: Roboto Slab is built on Roboto's skeleton, so slab headings add texture while sharing x-height and width with the body.
caution: Roboto Slab has no italics; use Roboto Italic for emphasis.

name: roboto-material
why: Material Design's baseline type scale uses Roboto alone and differentiates display/headline/title/body/label roles by size and weight.
caution: Reads as default Android; add brand character elsewhere (color, a display face).

name: inter-single-ui
why: One neo-grotesque family with strong weight contrast (700 vs 400) gives clear hierarchy with zero pairing risk; Inter's tall x-height holds up at small UI sizes.
caution: Use size and weight contrast generously or hierarchy collapses.

name: inter-tight-inter
why: Inter Tight is Inter respaced for display, so big headlines get tight, confident spacing while body stays in normally spaced Inter.
caution: Do not use Inter Tight for paragraphs; its spacing is for large sizes.

name: geist-dev
why: Geist and Geist Mono were drawn together; mono headings give an engineering voice and the proportional Geist body stays readable.
caution: Strongly associated with Vercel's aesthetic.

name: dm-serif-dm-sans
why: Colophon's DM family pairs a high-contrast display serif with a low-contrast geometric sans of matching x-height; contrast of classification within one design system.
caution: DM Serif Display has a single weight; never set it below ~24px.

name: alegreya-sans-alegreya
why: Both share Juan Pablo del Peral's calligraphic skeleton, so the humanist sans heading and dynamic serif body feel like one voice.
caution: Alegreya's small x-height needs a slightly larger body size on screen.

name: space-mono-space-grotesk
why: Space Grotesk is the proportional derivative of Space Mono; they share quirky details, and Typewolf shows them used together.
caution: Space Grotesk's quirks are distracting in long text; keep body passages short.

name: libre-franklin-libre-baskerville
why: A heavy American gothic over a transitional serif is the classic newspaper contrast; both have large x-heights so they sit together comfortably.
caution: Libre Baskerville is wide; keep body at 16-18px with moderate measure.

name: playfair-lato
why: High-contrast didone-style headings against a warm, low-contrast humanist sans maximizes classification contrast while both stay legible.
caution: Very common pairing; Playfair's hairlines break down below ~20px.

name: work-sans-bitter
why: A grotesque heading over a screen-optimized slab body: different classifications, similar large x-heights and low contrast, so they read as one texture.
caution: Bitter is dark; increase leading slightly (1.6) for long text.

name: montserrat-open-sans
why: Two sans serifs can pair when their construction differs: geometric Montserrat headings with humanist Open Sans body (font-matrix principle).
caution: Both are extremely common; the result is safe but generic.

name: oswald-source-sans
why: A condensed gothic display face gives punchy headlines in little width; a neutral humanist body keeps paragraphs readable.
caution: Oswald is uppercase-friendly but tiring in lowercase paragraphs; headings only.

name: schibsted-newsreader
why: Both were made for news reading; the heavy grotesque headline over an optical-size transitional body mirrors newspaper hierarchy.
caution: Let Newsreader's opsz follow size; display opsz at text size looks spindly.

name: literata-single-reading
why: Literata was designed for long-form reading (Google Play Books); one serif with weight contrast keeps a quiet, bookish page.
caution: Low heading contrast; use size (≥1.5x) for hierarchy.

name: fraunces-work-sans
why: Fraunces' soft 1970s old-style headings bring warmth; Work Sans's plain grotesque body stops the page from becoming costume.
caution: Avoid Fraunces' extreme WONK/SOFT settings in anything but the largest headings.

name: young-serif-rubik
why: A heavy old-style display serif with a softly rounded sans body shares a friendly, rounded tone while contrasting in classification.
caution: Young Serif has a single weight; keep it to headlines.

name: eb-garamond-single
why: A single Garamond with weight, small caps and italics gives a classic book page; Butterick notes one font with varied styles is often enough.
caution: Small x-height: set body ≥18px on screen and avoid for UI.

name: cormorant-jost
why: Both have small x-heights and refined proportions, so a delicate high-contrast Garamond heading sits naturally over Futura-like geometric body text.
caution: Cormorant is display-oriented; never use it below ~24px.

name: bodoni-moda-inter
why: Maximum stroke-contrast didone headlines against a zero-contrast neo-grotesque body: the fashion-magazine formula of drama plus neutrality.
caution: Bodoni hairlines vanish at small sizes and on low-res thumbnails.

name: cinzel-eb-garamond
why: Roman inscriptional capitals and a Renaissance garalde share classical roots, so the pair feels historically coherent.
caution: Cinzel is caps-only; keep headings short and letter-spaced.

name: marcellus-lato
why: A flared glyphic serif heading carries calm classicism; Lato's warm humanist body matches its gentle, low-key tone.
caution: Marcellus is a single weight; rely on size for hierarchy.

name: bebas-neue-inter
why: Tall all-caps condensed headlines pack impact into little width; a neutral neo-grotesque body stays out of the way.
caution: Bebas is uppercase only; never use it for sentences or body copy.

name: anton-roboto-thumbnail
why: Heavy condensed headlines stay legible when images are shrunk to thumbnails; Roboto supporting text is plain and readable.
caution: Anton has one weight; avoid lowercase sentences longer than a few words.

name: archivo-black-archivo
why: Archivo Black is the heavy display member of Archivo, giving strong weight contrast within one grotesque design.
caution: Archivo Black is wide; give headlines generous width.

name: space-mono-single-brutalist
why: Monospace throughout deliberately exposes structure, a brutalist web convention; weight is the only hierarchy cue.
caution: Keep body passages short and line length ≤ 70ch; mono text is slow to read.

name: unbounded-manrope
why: An extended display sans makes loud headlines; Manrope's compact semi-geometric body balances the width.
caution: Unbounded is very wide; limit headings to a few words.

name: league-gothic-libre-baskerville
why: A 1903 American condensed gothic over an 18th-c transitional serif recreates early 20th-century newspaper typography.
caution: League Gothic has one weight; set it large and in caps or title case.

name: alfa-slab-source-sans
why: A fat Egyptian display slab carries a 19th-c poster voice; a neutral humanist sans keeps supporting copy calm.
caution: Do not pair with another slab; one heavy voice per page.

name: abril-fatface-pt-sans
why: A heavy fat-face didone delivers drama; PT Sans's humanist body is sturdy and neutral for reading.
caution: Abril is display-only; never below ~28px.

name: shrikhand-nunito
why: A heavy, bouncy display face gives personality; Nunito's rounded terminals echo its softness in readable body text.
caution: Both are informal; avoid for serious or financial content.

name: fredoka-nunito
why: Two rounded sans serifs with similar large x-heights; concord pairing where the display face is just bubblier.
caution: Concord pairs need clear weight/size contrast or they look like a mistake.

name: rubik-karla
why: Rubik's softly rounded grotesque headings and Karla's quirky grotesque body share a casual, approachable tone with distinct textures.
caution: Two sans serifs: keep heading weight ≥700 so the roles are clear.

name: poppins-lora
why: Geometric sans headings over a calligraphic contemporary serif body: clean modern headings, warm readable text.
caution: Poppins' large x-height dwarfs Lora at equal sizes; keep headings clearly larger.

name: plus-jakarta-single
why: A single geometric sans with strong weight contrast gives a contemporary product voice without pairing risk.
caution: Widely used by startups; add brand distinction via color or imagery.

name: lexend-atkinson
why: Both families were designed around reading research and letter differentiation; large x-heights and open forms keep everything legible.
caution: Lexend is wide; watch heading line breaks in narrow layouts.

name: merriweather-source-sans-civic
why: These are the U.S. Web Design System's default serif and sans tokens; a sturdy screen serif heading over a clear humanist sans body.
caution: Merriweather is optically large; scale it down relative to the sans.

name: public-sans-single
why: Public Sans is built for neutral, accessible interfaces; one family with weight contrast keeps forms calm and consistent.
caution: Neutral to the point of anonymity; fine for services, weak for brand.

name: lora-source-sans
why: Calligraphic serif headings add warmth; a clean humanist sans body keeps reading easy on screens.
caution: Lora's italics are quite cursive; use sparingly for emphasis.

name: zilla-slab-fira-sans
why: A contemporary slab headline over a humanist sans body: slab serifs add editorial personality, Fira Sans keeps it technical and clear.
caution: Zilla Slab bold is idiosyncratic; avoid it for long subheads.

name: instrument-serif-sans
why: A condensed high-contrast display serif with its sibling neo-grotesque: a contemporary editorial pairing from one design house.
caution: Instrument Serif has one weight; use it only at display sizes.

name: josefin-sans-crimson-pro
why: Both have small x-heights and refined proportions; a 1920s-flavored geometric heading over an old-style book serif reads vintage and elegant.
caution: Small x-heights: raise body size to 18px+.

name: league-spartan-libre-baskerville
why: Echoes the classic Futura + Baskerville pairing: geometric 20th-c sans headings over an 18th-c transitional serif body.
caution: League Spartan's black weights are very heavy; use 700-800 for headlines.

name: syne-dm-sans
why: Syne's heavy, widened display weights are deliberately eccentric; a clean geometric body sans keeps information readable.
caution: Syne's width changes with weight; test heading line breaks.

name: big-shoulders-barlow
why: Both draw on signage traditions (Chicago and California); the condensed display headline and the plain grotesk body feel related but distinct.
caution: Big Shoulders Display is for large sizes only.

name: barlow-condensed-barlow
why: Width contrast within one family: condensed headings save horizontal space while sharing Barlow's details with the body.
caution: Condensed widths are not for body text.

name: bricolage-figtree
why: An expressive, ink-trapped grotesque headline gives personality; Figtree's clean geometric body is calm and friendly.
caution: Two sans serifs: lean on Bricolage's heavy weights to separate roles.

name: great-vibes-eb-garamond
why: A formal script for one or two words of heading/accent over a classical Garamond body keeps the romance while the text stays readable.
caution: Never set Great Vibes in all caps or for more than a short line.

name: pacifico-lato
why: A brush script supplies a single loud personality; Lato's warm neutral sans carries everything else.
caution: Pacifico is over-used; restrict to a logo or one headline.

name: caveat-karla
why: Handwriting headings or annotations add a personal touch; Karla's quirky grotesque body matches the informal tone.
caution: Never use Caveat for body text, buttons or UI labels.

name: unifraktur-libre-caslon
why: A fraktur masthead over a Caslon body evokes traditional newspapers and printed heritage, where blackletter titles met old-style text.
caution: Blackletter only for a few words; never all caps.

name: press-start-space-mono
why: Pixel display headlines and a retro-futurist monospace body share a computer-native aesthetic.
caution: Press Start 2P is unreadable small; set at multiples of 8px and ≥16px.

name: jetbrains-mono-inter-docs
why: Mono headings set a developer tone and double as the code face; both have tall x-heights and low contrast, so they align visually.
caution: Use the mono for headings and code only, not paragraphs.

name: old-standard-single-academic
why: Reproduces a late-19th-c 'modern' used in scientific publishing; one family keeps a coherent period page.
caution: Italic exists only at 400 and hairlines are thin on screens; set body ≥18px.

name: public-sans-source-serif
why: A sturdy sans heading above a calm serif reading face.
caution: Keep sufficient size and weight contrast between heading and body.

name: inter-tight-literata
why: Compact headings leave room for spacious long-form copy.
caution: Keep sufficient size and weight contrast between heading and body.

name: schibsted-noto-serif
why: Clear news headings pair with restrained serif body text.
caution: Keep sufficient size and weight contrast between heading and body.

name: atkinson-source-serif
why: Distinctive sans letterforms clarify headings over a readable serif body.
caution: Keep sufficient size and weight contrast between heading and body.

name: anton-libre-franklin
why: Dense display capitals contrast with an open practical body face.
caution: Use display only for short headings at 40 px or larger; keep the body face for captions and long copy.

name: bebas-source-serif
why: Tall narrow display type contrasts with an editorial serif.
caution: Use display only for short headings at 40 px or larger; keep the body face for captions and long copy.

name: oswald-public-sans
why: Condensed headlines leave a steady sans face for explanations.
caution: Use display only for short headings at 40 px or larger; keep the body face for captions and long copy.

name: bungee-figtree
why: Sign-painting display forms anchor friendly readable body copy.
caution: Use display only for short headings at 40 px or larger; keep the body face for captions and long copy.

name: barlow-condensed-newsreader
why: Narrow industrial headings contrast with fluid editorial text.
caution: Use display only for short headings at 40 px or larger; keep the body face for captions and long copy.

name: big-shoulders-work-sans
why: Strong vertical headlines pair with unobtrusive sans body copy.
caution: Use display only for short headings at 40 px or larger; keep the body face for captions and long copy.

name: fraunces-atkinson
why: Expressive soft serif headings sit above clear accessible body forms.
caution: Use display only for short headings at 40 px or larger; keep the body face for captions and long copy.

name: archivo-black-karla
why: Heavy compact headings contrast with a lightly textured sans body.
caution: Use display only for short headings at 40 px or larger; keep the body face for captions and long copy.

name: monoton-space-grotesk
why: Striped display lettering contrasts with a clean geometric body.
caution: Use display only for short headings at 40 px or larger; keep the body face for captions and long copy.

name: grenze-ibm-plex-sans
why: Blackletter headings meet a neutral contemporary reading voice.
caution: Use display only for short headings at 40 px or larger; keep the body face for captions and long copy.

name: permanent-marker-geist
why: Handmade marker headings contrast with precise interface text.
caution: Use display only for short headings at 40 px or larger; keep the body face for captions and long copy.

name: shrikhand-source-code
why: Rounded exuberant display lettering contrasts with disciplined monospaced copy.
caution: Use display only for short headings at 40 px or larger; keep the body face for captions and long copy.
